# References {.unnumbered}

Every page of this book names its sources where it uses them. This
chapter collects them in one place: first the open textbooks and
resources the book is built on, then all papers and books cited on any
page (checked against PubMed or CrossRef), then databases, datasets and
software, and finally the further reading and watching suggested for
each session. "Cited in" links back to the pages that use each source.

## The open sources this book is built on

This book draws its narrative content from fully open sources,
supplemented by original writing. None of the sources below restrict
commercial use. Every page names which of them it used.

- **Dive into Deep Learning.** Zhang, A., Lipton, Z. C., Li, M., & Smola,
  A. J. <https://d2l.ai>. [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
  Primary source for every machine-learning session. Adapted material from
  this source is, per that license, shared here under the same terms.
- **Wikipedia.** <https://en.wikipedia.org>. [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
  Conceptual and algorithmic depth for the bioinformatics sessions, and
  occasional historical notes elsewhere. Never assigned as reading
  directly, but synthesized into this book's own bounded pages (see the
  Welcome page for why).
- **EMBL-EBI Training.** <https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/>. [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
  The practical, tool-use layer for databases and sequence alignment.
- **bibook.** Käll, L. <https://github.com/statisticalbiotechnology/bibook>.
  [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Notebook code
  implementing classical bioinformatics algorithms (pairwise alignment,
  MSA, and more), adapted with attribution.
- **NCBI Bookshelf.** <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/>. Public domain
  (US government work). The BLAST algorithm and database practicalities,
  including the BLAST® Help manual.
- **RCSB PDB-101.** <https://pdb101.rcsb.org/>. [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
  (the PDB-101 educational tier; general rcsb.org article text is
  separately copyrighted and is not used here).
- **A Byte of Python.** Swaroop, C. H. <https://python.swaroopch.com/>.
  [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Python
  fundamentals and object-oriented programming.

## What isn't reused, and why

- **Magnus Ekman's *Learning Deep Learning*** and **Jonathan Pevsner's
  *Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics*** were this course's previously
  assigned textbooks. Both are under conventional copyright. Nothing from
  either is reproduced here; some pages credit Ekman's book (and the
  teachers' own earlier lecture slides) as an internal source of ideas,
  and any resemblance in topic ordering is because these books teach the
  same standard material.
- **Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville's *Deep Learning*** is free to read
  online but not licensed for reuse or redistribution, so it is treated
  like the two textbooks above.
- **Michael Nielsen's *Neural Networks and Deep Learning*** is CC BY-NC:
  freely reusable for non-commercial teaching, but an earlier draft that
  used it was switched to *Dive into Deep Learning* throughout, to keep one
  license without a non-commercial restriction across the whole book.
